diagnosed_skill_and_repair.overall_diagnosis: Build failures in fix-build-google-auto are primarily due to Maven dependency and plugin resolution/execution problems under legacy CI/JDK constraints (notably TLS/SSL transport failures to Maven Central and ensuing missing classes from unresolved artifacts). Secondary issues involve multi-module reactor behavior and non-ideal ordering/mixing of lifecycle phases and plugin goals (e.g., go-offline/test/clean), which can mask root causes and cascade failures across modules. The skill gaps are mostly around practical troubleshooting for legacy environments (JDK7/old Maven), repository/protocol configuration, and concrete plugin/dependency repair techniques (pinning versions, exclusions, and safe temporary skips).

skills.name: maven-build-lifecycle
skills.heading: Maven Build Lifecycle
skills.diagnosis: Command usage and logs indicate confusion/fragility around mixing lifecycle phases with plugin goals and multi-module reactor behavior (e.g., go-offline/test/clean ordering, verify vs install impacts, reactor cascades and banned modules). The skill is largely a phase list and lacks pragmatic guidance for diagnosing reactor failures, resuming builds, and choosing correct phase/goal sequences for CI, especially in multi-module projects with integration-test/invoker steps.
skills.repair_instruction: Add a lifecycle debugging subsection: explain why clean should typically precede compile/test and how mixing plugin goals (e.g., dependency:go-offline) with phases affects outcomes; provide recommended CI command patterns (e.g., go-offline before build, then clean verify/install as appropriate). Include multi-module reactor troubleshooting: reading the reactor summary, isolating modules with -pl/-am, resuming with -rf, and understanding how early-module failures cause downstream skips/bans (and when install is required for modules/tests that expect artifacts in the local repo).

skills.name: maven-dependency-management
skills.heading: Maven Dependency Management
skills.diagnosis: Failures include dependency descriptor transfer errors (TLS/SSL) and downstream compilation/runtime missing-class symptoms (e.g., NoClassDefFoundError for auto-common/MoreElements) consistent with unresolved or misaligned transitive dependencies. The skill covers basic dependency declaration but lacks practical guidance for diagnosing resolution failures in constrained/legacy CI, fixing transitive dependency mismatches, and applying cross-JDK compatibility shims (adding/replacing JDK-removed artifacts, excluding obsolete deps) commonly needed in these builds.
skills.repair_instruction: Add practical troubleshooting guidance for: (1) repository transport/TLS resolution failures (how to confirm what failed with -X/-U and dependency:tree/resolve, and when to use mirrors/settings vs POM); (2) interpreting missing-class errors as dependency graph problems and fixing them with explicit deps, exclusions, and version alignment; (3) using <dependencyManagement> to force consistent versions across multi-module projects; (4) cross-JDK compatibility patterns (replacing removed JDK-provided artifacts, adding javax/jakarta annotation APIs when needed, excluding obsolete tools.jar-era deps). Provide examples for dependency:tree-driven diagnosis, an exclusion snippet, and a dependencyManagement alignment snippet.

skills.name: maven-plugin-configuration
skills.heading: Maven Plugin Configuration
skills.diagnosis: Evidence repeatedly shows Maven plugin resolution and plugin execution failures (dependency:go-offline/resolve-plugins, enforcer, surefire, invoker, compiler/annotation processing). The skill mentions pluginRepositories but lacks actionable troubleshooting for plugin resolution vs dependency resolution, legacy TLS/JDK compatibility, pinning compatible plugin versions, and handling plugin classpath/transitive dependency issues that can surface as NoClassDefFoundError during build steps.
skills.repair_instruction: Add a focused troubleshooting section covering: (1) differentiating pluginRepositories vs repositories and when to use settings.xml mirrors vs POM changes; (2) diagnosing plugin transfer/TLS failures in legacy environments (e.g., old JDKs/Maven) including repository URL/protocol checks and when environment flags/settings are required; (3) overriding/pinning plugin versions via <pluginManagement> for JDK compatibility; (4) excluding/overriding problematic transitive plugin dependencies when plugin classpath failures occur; (5) CI-stability controls for common plugins (surefire/invoker/enforcer) including safe, profile-guarded skips (e.g., -DskipTests, enforcer.skip, invoker.skip) and criteria for when temporary skips are acceptable. Include concrete POM snippets for pluginManagement overrides and profile-based executions.

repair_outcome.analysis: A skill was localized and rewritten, but the comparable method-skill run still failed; likely causes are insufficient repair content or downstream model execution limits.
